name: trade_size_clustering_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Institutional orders in Indian equities are often split into round-lot sizes (multiples of 100 or 500 shares) via TWAP/VWAP algorithms. When we detect clusters of trades at consistent round-lot sizes within a rolling window, it signals institutional accumulation or distribution. The inefficiency persists because: (1) Indian brokers' TWAP algos use predictable lot sizes, (2) retail traders trade odd lots and small sizes making institutional clusters detectable, (3) the signal requires tick-level trade reconstruction which most retail platforms don't support. We trade in the direction of detected institutional flow, expecting price to move toward the institutional target.
mechanism: Order flow imbalance between aggressive buyers and sellers creates short-term price pressure. When buy-side aggression exceeds sell-side by a threshold, the order book tilts and market makers adjust their quotes upward. This creates a 15-45 second drift before the book rebalances as new limit orders arrive to capture the improved price.

indicators.name: round_lot_ratio
indicators.formula: count(trades where qty % 100 == 0) / count(all_trades) over 5-min rolling window

indicators.name: large_trade_pct
indicators.formula: sum(qty where qty > 5 * median_trade_size) / sum(all_qty) over 5-min window

indicators.name: cluster_direction
indicators.formula: sign(sum(signed_qty * (qty >= 100)) over 5-min window) where signed_qty = qty if trade_at_ask else -qty

filters.vix_filter: no filter (institutional flow persists across volatility regimes)

weaknesses: Tick-level trade data in India is expensive and not available via standard Zerodha API. NSE TBT data feed required, adding infrastructure cost.
Institutional algos are increasingly randomizing trade sizes to avoid detection, directly degrading the round_lot_ratio signal quality.
False positives from retail traders who also trade round lots (especially in lower-priced stocks where 100 shares is a small notional).
prior_art: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012) 'Flow Toxicity and Liquidity' (VPIN). Hasbrouck (2007) 'Empirical Market Microstructure' covers trade classification. Kyle (1985) 'Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading' provides theoretical basis for informed trader detection.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; order book data integration. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
